payload.title: Concentration-dependent cytotoxicity of three repurposed kinase inhibitors in primary human hepatocytes from six donors
payload.abstract: Predicting hepatotoxicity before a repurposing candidate reaches the clinic remains difficult, and immortalised lines can underestimate injury because they lack full metabolic competence. Cryopreserved primary human hepatocytes from six donors were plated in collagen-coated plates and allowed to recover for 24 hours before treatment. Cells were exposed to sunitinib, pazopanib or regorafenib for 48 hours across a nine-point concentration range. Viability was measured by cellular ATP content and normalised to vehicle control. Mean IC50 values were 11.2, 24.8 and 8.6 micromolar respectively, with a roughly four-fold spread across donors. Donor variation exceeded plate-to-plate variation for all three compounds. Primary hepatocytes retained albumin secretion throughout the exposure period.
